options.counterfactual: Every norm-bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, by an established theorem applicable to the definitions in this problem.
options.approach: Identify the precise theorem and verify its hypotheses against the stated annihilator and finiteness conditions. If it applies to noncommuting sequences, use it to conclude that the required absence of a least upper bound is impossible.

options.approach: Seek a proof of the sequential completeness assertion using projection joins and finite continuous dimension. Focus on constructing an upper bound for a noncommuting increasing sequence rather than treating projection completeness as sufficient.

options.counterfactual: Every norm-bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, by an established theorem applicable to the definitions in this problem.
options.approach: Investigate whether every finite AW*-factor admits an order-preserving representation in a monotone complete algebra whose increasing suprema remain inside the represented factor. Such a representation would provide the missing supremum directly.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace can assign the same strictly positive value to every successive difference of a bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor.
options.approach: Search for a construction of positive elements with bounded partial sums and quasitrace values uniformly bounded away from zero. Determine separately whether their partial sums lack a least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace can assign the same strictly positive value to every successive difference of a bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor.
options.approach: Assume one witness exists and examine scaling, compression to corners, and normalization of order intervals. Determine whether these operations generate every increment below a universal endpoint.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace can assign the same strictly positive value to every successive difference of a bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor.
options.approach: Investigate quasitracial ultraproducts of finite configurations having increasingly many constant positive increments. Check both whether the resulting algebra is a finite AW*-factor and whether the infinite sequence has no least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the summands of any positive series with bounded partial sums to numbers tending to zero, even when the ambient algebra is not monotone complete.
options.approach: Seek a quasitracial exhaustion theorem stating that bounded positive partial sums force the individual quasitrace values to tend to zero. Such a theorem would exclude the prescribed constant increments without using the AW*-factor assumptions.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the summands of any positive series with bounded partial sums to numbers tending to zero, even when the ambient algebra is not monotone complete.
options.approach: Use spectral cutoffs to turn a hypothetical counterexample into infinitely many projections of uniformly positive quasitrace whose finite sums are uniformly bounded. Look for a dimension-theoretic obstruction to such a projection family.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the summands of any positive series with bounded partial sums to numbers tending to zero, even when the ambient algebra is not monotone complete.
options.approach: Investigate whether matrix amplification and the 2-quasitrace extension yield a lower estimate for the quasitrace of positive sums. An estimate growing with the number of uniformly positive summands would contradict boundedness of their partial sums.
